headline: PTI chairman rejects Barrister Saif's claims, says all efforts made to meet Imran Khan
subheadline: Barrister Gohar says party repeatedly denied access to incarcerated founder
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Gohar terms Barrister Saif’s claims false, baseless.
Says courts, negotiations used to seek meeting.
Access to Imran was condition during talks.

PESHAWAR: PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Monday rejected party leader Barrister Muhammad Ali Saif’s claims, saying the party had made every possible effort to secure a meeting with incarcerated founder Imran Khan.

Speaking to the media in Peshawar, Gohar termed as “baseless” Saif’s assertion that PTI leaders had failed to meet Imran despite being offered an opportunity to do so.

“We made every possible effort to meet the PTI founder through the courts and negotiations, but despite all our efforts, we were not allowed even a single meeting,” he said.

Gohar said access to Imran had also been one of the party’s conditions during the negotiation process.

He rejected the assertions made by Saif during his interview, saying: “All of Barrister Saif’s claims are false. I reject them.”

Saif, during an interview on Geo News programme Jirga, had said that Allama Raja Nasir Abbas was in direct contact with important figures in the establishment, but maintained that those contacts were not aimed at securing Imran’s release.

Separately, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja linked any party decision on the proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment to a meeting with Imran.

Raja also expressed his inability to exercise control over PTI’s social media.

PTI dismisses reports of internal divisions

Moreover, PTI today dismissed reports of internal divisions, saying the entire party remained united behind its founder, his ideology and mission.

In a statement issued after a meeting of its political committee, the party said there was no grouping or division within its ranks and that its leaders and workers would continue their struggle towards their shared objectives.

The committee also discussed the country’s political situation, inflation and law and order, according to the statement.

It demanded the immediate release of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister, provincial assembly speaker and other detained parliamentarians, describing their detention as illegal.

PTI said keeping elected representatives in custody was an affront to democratic values and the public mandate.

The political committee expressed concern over reports that Imran and his wife Bushra Bibi had been shifted to hospital without their families being taken into confidence.

It demanded immediate implementation of the Supreme Court’s order regarding medical treatment for the PTI founder and called for his family to be regularly informed about his health.

The committee also demanded that Imran’s family be allowed to meet and visit him, while appropriate medical facilities and family meetings should also be ensured for Bushra Bibi.

PTI also condemned the arrest of Imran’s sisters and their treatment in custody, demanding their immediate release and permission for them to meet the former premier.

The committee raised concerns over the arrests of MNA Adil Bazai and other party leaders and workers, demanding the immediate release of all those detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO).

It said no individual should be subjected to retaliation over political differences.

PTI also condemned raids and vandalism at the residences of Omar Ayub, Sher Ali Arbab and Shah Ahad, saying targeting the homes and families of political opponents was condemnable.

Separately, the political committee expressed concern over the increasing incidents of terrorism in the country, describing the menace as a serious threat requiring effective and concerted measures.

The party said protecting citizens’ lives and property was a fundamental responsibility of the state.

It added that actions against terrorism should not be used for political retaliation.

headline: Mohammad Amir ‘registers' as UK national for Afghanistan Premier League draft
subheadline: PCB is unlikely to issue NOCs to its players for the tournament, suggest media reports
author: Web Desk
article_text:
KARACHI: Former Pakistan pacer Mohammad Amir has registered as a UK national for the Afghanistan Premier League (APL) draft, scheduled to take place in Dubai on Tuesday, according to media reports.

Amir, who currently resides in England and has acquired British citizenship, has been listed as a UK national in the draft register, with Pakistan mentioned as his country of residence. He has been placed in the Platinum category.

Amir has represented Pakistan in 36 Tests, 61 One-Day Internationals (ODIs) and 62 T20 Internationals. His last appearance for the national side came against Ireland during the ICC Men's T20 World Cup in Lauderhill, Florida, in June 2024.

Registering as a UK national could also give Amir an advantage regarding his availability for the APL, as he may not require a No-Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), unlike his former Pakistan teammates.

Meanwhile, more than 30 Pakistani cricketers, including Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Hasan Ali, Shan Masood, Abdullah Shafique, Faheem Ashraf and Imad Wasim, have registered for the draft.

However, the participation of Pakistani players remains uncertain amid reported diplomatic tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan. Media reports suggest that the PCB is unlikely to issue NOCs to its players for the tournament.

The Afghanistan Cricket Board's (ACB) draft register has also clarified that the participation of Pakistani players is subject to obtaining NOCs from the PCB.

The APL will feature five teams, with each franchise permitted to register a maximum of 18 players, comprising 11-12 Afghanistan players and six to seven overseas recruits.

The players have been divided into five categories, with Platinum players set to receive $100,000, followed by $65,000 for Diamond, $40,000 for Gold, $20,000 for Silver and $10,000 for Emerging players.

Each franchise will have a total player purse ranging from $650,000 to $750,000.

headline: Taylor Swift shares sweet anecdote about friendship with Abigail Anderson
subheadline: Taylor Swift speaks about finding instant connection with childhood bestfriend
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Taylor Swift and Abigail Anderson share a decades-long friendship and the pop icon looked back to the beginning of their lifelong bond, in a new panel talk.

The 36-year-old star appeared for a conversation about Toy Story 5 and spoke about friendship, saying, it's "about finding someone who's the same genre of weird and silly as you are and what just why Bonnie and Blaise's story resonated with me so much. You know when I moved to Nashville when I was 14, you know, you're the new kid in school, you're like who who should I be friends with, these girls are cool. These girls are cool."

However, among all the cool and nice girls, "there was one girl named Abigail and she even has curly hair to like blaze and the two of us all we wanted to do was talk in Napoleon Dynamite voices and we still do this and like it's something our husbands have to put up with. And so it's just like what are you doing today?" Swift said, emulating the voice, "I don't know. What are you doing? Oh, are you playing with your cute kid? Yeah. Yeah, what's the problem with that? And so it's like, you know when you find that person who just completely sees you for the strange little genre that is you at your purest. That's that that hit me so hard watching the film."

Swifties loved getting an insight into one of the friendships the Grammy winner has written multiple songs about, and commented, "this was a documentary."

One noted, "That’s her DIBBLES VOICE!!!!" referring to the pet name for Swift's cat Olivia Benson.

While a third chimed in, "That's such a sweet friendship. I love that they still share the same silly jokes after all these years their husbands must be used to it by now," and "Abigail mention love their friendship!" wrote another.

headline: Learjet 60 crashes in Florida: Here's what went wrong
subheadline: All nine on board killed in Learjet 60 crash
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A Learjet 60 carrying nine people crashed into a roadway in Palm Beach County on Sunday, November 1, afternoon, killing everyone on board and leaving a massive crater near a mobile home park in what officials call a “cataclysmic” Florida plane crash.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. Dashcam confirmed that the jet, which departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was bound for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, went down at about 12:50 p.m. ET near Cresthaven.

Dashcam footage revealed the aircraft falling nose-first before exploding into a fireball, narrowly missing cars and homes.

Air traffic control audio captured the crew’s final moments. The pilot initially reported icing conditions, an outside air temperature of -47 degrees Celsius, and moderate turbulence.

Moments later, the pilot declared “Mayday, mayday,” reporting a descent rate of 10,000 ft per minute before warning: “We’re going to crash into the ground.”

Flight tracking data reported the descent rate exceeded 32,000 ft per minute at one point.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said: “It was a cataclysmic plane crash. It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road.”

Officials said there were no immediate reports of injuries on the ground.

About 600 residents near the crash site were evacuated to two shelters because debris blocked the entrance to a mobile home park, said Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores.

The National Transportation Safety Board has opened an investigation. The crash is the deadliest involving a Learjet 60 and the second-deadliest U.S. plane crash this year.

headline: King Charles' health concerns put William, Catherine's key plans on hold
subheadline: Prince William, Princess Kate turn down big offer for King Charles' sake
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prince William and Princess Kate made key changes to their plans amid concerns for cancer-stricken King Charles.

The Prince and Princess of Wales are the most important members of the monarch's team. On King's behalf, the couple represents the royal family at several distinguished events.

After Catherine announced that she is in remission from cancer, fans expected a joint royal tour of the two in Australia. Though the future Queen went on a meaningful tour of Italy, this year the Waleses' reported Australia tour was not made possible.

READ MORE: Prince William moves on from Harry with special new replacement

Now, sources claimed that the real reason behind this delay is King Charles' health issues.

According to New Idea, "William and Kate have yet to accept the Aussie PM’s invite, but Robert Irwin wants them down under just as much as any Aussie.

"William’s promised to bring the kids to the Irwin zoo one day, and Robert takes every opportunity to remind him of that."

It has been almost 10 years since the Waleses travelled to Down Under as the firm prioritised King Charles' maximum tours, keeping in mind his growing age and cancer treatment.

READ MORE: King Charles finally gets his umbrella — watch his hilarious reaction

"It’s all unnecessary, of course, because William and Kate have Australia on their schedule every year, but something always comes up that forces them to push it back," an insider added. "The King’s health has been a huge factor stopping them from committing to a big tour."

headline: New mechanism allowed govt to keep petrol price Rs15 cheaper: minister
subheadline: Ali Pervaiz says refineries absorbed increase as fuel import premiums surged
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Petrol premium surged from $5 to $20.
Refineries helped absorb Rs15 per litre increase.
Minister says Nov gas arrangements already secured.

ISLAMABAD: Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said on Monday that the government’s revised pricing mechanism and cooperation from local refineries enabled it to keep petrol around Rs15 per litre cheaper than international market rates amid the US-Iran war.

Speaking about the recent changes to the petrol pricing mechanism, Malik said the regional conflict had sharply increased costs associated with fuel imports, including freight, insurance and other logistics expenses.

He said the premium on petrol stood at around $5 per barrel before the war but subsequently surged to $20 per barrel.

The minister said subsequent PSO tenders showed premiums climbing further to around $25-$30 per barrel and even higher as regional conditions deteriorated.

Malik said the government worked with local refineries to deal with the situation and contain the impact on consumers without disrupting the availability of imported petrol.

Around 70% of the country’s petrol requirement comes from the international market while locally produced petrol accounts for about 30%, according to the minister.

He said the government had to ensure that any intervention did not make imported petrol commercially unviable and consequently lead to supply shortages.

“I am grateful that they listened to our appeal and absorbed roughly a Rs15 increase that was coming due for petrol on Friday, helping the government maintain prices,” Malik said, referring to local refineries.

He said the arrangement had allowed petrol to be kept around Rs15 per litre cheaper than international market rates, adding that refineries were absorbing a burden of roughly Rs15 billion per month.

Malik said international market prices were now declining, expressing hope that the trend would lead to further improvement for consumers.

How revised petrol pricing works

The federal cabinet approved changes to the petrol pricing mechanism on October 30 amid volatility caused by the US-Iran war.

Under the revised formula, the import price of petrol is determined on the basis of the actual import cost of the relevant PSO cargo. If that cost is unavailable for daily pricing, the premium, incidentals and customs duty of the last available cargo are used instead.

For local refineries, the government has temporarily fixed the premium, incidentals and customs duty used in calculating the ex-refinery petrol price at their March 7, 2026 — pre-war — levels for 30 days.

The difference between the import price and the resulting ex-refinery price is to be surrendered by refineries under the petroleum levy account, with the resulting benefit passed on through a corresponding reduction in the petrol price.

The government has also introduced a short-term adjustment to smooth petrol price movements, incorporating the benefit arising from a premium differential into petrol prices at a rate of $2.950 per barrel per day.

Govt says no fuel shortage

Meanwhile, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said there was no fuel shortage in Pakistan and the country’s requirements were being met.

Malik also rejected reports that LPG prices had climbed as high as Rs700 per kilogramme.

On gas supplies, the petroleum minister said arrangements for November were already in place, while the government was making arrangements to meet requirements for December and January.

headline: Russell Brand's defence makes shocking claim over 2023 documentary
subheadline: Russell's lawyer also talked about how the allegations affected his family life
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Russell Brand's trial took new turn after his lawyer made strong claims about a documentary that first brought many allegations against him into the public eye.

During his final speech in court, Brand's lawyer Ian Winter KC said the 2023 Channel 4 Dispatches programme affected the case before it even reached trial.

He claimed the documentary encouraged women to come forward and changed the way people looked at Brand. He told the jury that the programme "poisoned the well of justice".

READ MORE: Russell Brand trial hears new claims from third accuser

Winter, however, also said that the women who are involved in the case were influenced by what they saw in the documentary.

He questioned how their claims can be treated as fully separate from the programme.

Brand is currently on trial at Southwark Crown Court over seven charges, which including rape and sexual assault but he, moreover, denied all those charges.

The lawyer also asked the jury to not to judge Brand for his personal life, sharing that having relationships with many women was not a crime.

READ MORE: Russell Brand leans on one person during major assault case

Winter also spoke about how the allegations affected Brand's family life as well as he reminded the court that a hospital refused to let him visit his baby son after his heart surgery in 2023.

headline: Buccaneers' shutout win over Falcons keeps NFC South hopes alive
subheadline: The Falcons lost to a Bucs team that didn’t complete a single pass, falling in a Week 8 matchup on Sunday afternoon in Florida
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Atlanta Falcons headed into Week 8 with a chance to dominate the NFC South but were instead shut out by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to fall to 3-5 for the season.

One week after they pulled off a surprise upset win over the red-hot San Francisco 49ers, the Falcons lost to a Bucs team that didn’t complete a single pass on offense.

On Atlanta’s side, Michael Penix Jr had a brutal game, throwing four interceptions just a few days after winning the NFC Offensive Player of the Week.

The heavy rain didn’t help Penix or the Falcons' defense, which looked a step slower attempting to stop Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Despite an 0-4 start, Tampa Bay is now poised to seize control of the NFC South at 3-5 with wins over the Falcons and the Carolina Panthers in back-to-back weeks.

As the Panthers head into NFL Week 9, they remain first in the division, but their lead over the Bucs is just half a game.

What are NFC South standings heading into NFL Week 9?

Carolina Panthers (3-4)

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5)

Atlanta Falcons (3-5)

New Orleans Saints (2-5)

In NFL Week 9, the Falcons will play the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain, on Sunday, November 8.

The Bucs will travel to Chicago to play against the Bears on Sunday Night Football.

Whereas the Panthers will host the Denver Broncos on Sunday afternoon, while the New Orleans Saints are back in action after a week off and will play host to the Cleveland Browns.

headline: Olivia Rodrigo shows love to Phoebe Bridgers at Lost Tour amid her own tour
subheadline: Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers share a sweet bond of mutual admiration
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Olivia Rodrigo might be headlining her Unraveled Tour herself but she herself is a music fan inside and takes the time to enjoy music as a fan as well.

During her day off from her own tour, the 23-year-old pop superstar was found in the audience at Phoebe Bridger's final North American show of The Lost Tour in Los Angeles.

Since the Scott Street hitmaker has a strict no-phone policy at her shows, there were no pictures of the drop dead songstress, but many attendees took to social media and reported the event.

READ MORE: Phoebe Bridgers overwhelms fans with special guest during Lost Tour

Social media went wild about their two musicians interacting, writing, "MY GIRLLSSSSS," and "WHAT OMG."

While a third chimed in, "I want them to work together !" and "MY PARENTS."

Another added, "I'm in tears-" and "PHOEBELIVIA," gushed another.
